subject: Science

book.title: Curiosity
book.officialStructureEvidence: NCERT textbook portal lists Curiosity for Class VI Science with 12 chapter files; current 2026-27 index corroborates titles/order.
book.sourcePolicy: Chapter titles/order are curriculum mapping metadata. KirthiVerse teaching text, examples, questions, hints and remediation are independently authored; no textbook prose, figures or exercise questions are reproduced.

chapters.title: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
A Journey through States of Water
Methods of Separation in Everyday Life

chapter1Topics.title: Curiosity, observation and scientific questions
competencies: distinguish observation from assumption
turn an observation into a useful question
identify questions that can be investigated with evidence
misconceptions: treating an opinion as an observation
assuming every why-question can be answered by one simple experiment

chapter1Topics.title: Testable explanations and fair investigations
competencies: propose a testable explanation
identify what to change and what to observe
keep important comparison conditions similar
recognise that a prediction can be wrong without the investigation being useless
misconceptions: changing several factors at once
treating a hypothesis as a proven fact

chapter1Topics.title: Recording evidence, analysing results and revising ideas
competencies: record results honestly
compare results with a prediction
draw a conclusion limited to the evidence
revise an explanation when evidence disagrees
misconceptions: changing results to match a prediction
calling an unexpected result a failed experiment

chapter1CompletionRule: CHAPTER1_KIKI_TEACHING_SLICE_COMPLETE requires all three mapped inquiry topics to include independently authored teaching, a worked investigation, misconception handling, linked practice/assessment, remediation/mastery evidence, deterministic QA, offline coverage and release regression coverage.

chapter2Topics.title: Observing diversity and describing variation
competencies: compare living things using multiple observable characteristics
record similarities and differences systematically
limit generalisations to the observed sample
misconceptions: a few examples represent every member of a group
one obvious characteristic fully describes diversity

chapter2Topics.title: Classification and simple branching keys
competencies: group using stated observable criteria
apply one criterion consistently
follow and construct simple branching keys
recognise that different useful criteria can produce different groupings
misconceptions: classification can use unstated preference
there is only one perfect grouping for every purpose

chapter2Topics.title: Organisms, habitats and evidence-aware adaptation reasoning
competencies: separate observed trait from inferred function
relate habitat evidence to cautious functional hypotheses
identify additional evidence needed
use privacy- and conservation-aware observation practices
misconceptions: trait function is directly observed
trait plus habitat proves exact cause or evolutionary history

chapter2CompletionRule: CHAPTER2_KIKI_TEACHING_SLICE_COMPLETE requires all three mapped diversity topics to include independently authored teaching, evidence-aware examples, misconception handling, linked practice/assessment, remediation/mastery evidence, deterministic QA, offline coverage and release regression coverage.

chapter3Topics.title: Food diversity and what nutrients do
competencies: describe broad nutrient/component roles
recognise food diversity across cultural meals
avoid diagnosing nutrient status from one meal
misconceptions: one food must contain every nutrient
one nutrient makes a food or person morally good/bad
one meal diagnoses a deficiency
safetyBoundary: no body-shaming
no deficiency diagnosis
no calorie prescription

chapter3Topics.title: Building balanced meals and mindful routines
competencies: improve hypothetical meal variety
include hydration reasoning
recognise individual needs vary
misconceptions: balanced means identical plates
balance means restriction or skipping meals
all children should follow one calorie target
safetyBoundary: no weight-loss plans
no fasting targets
no universal calorie targets

chapter3Topics.title: Food information, hygiene and evidence-aware choices
competencies: separate label facts from marketing claims
describe basic food hygiene
escalate allergy/medical diet concerns appropriately
misconceptions: marketing phrases prove health outcomes
children should self-test allergens
supplements can be self-prescribed as treatment
safetyBoundary: no allergy self-testing
no supplement treatment advice
medical dietary needs escalate to trusted adult and qualified healthcare guidance

chapter3CompletionRule: CHAPTER3_KIKI_TEACHING_SLICE_COMPLETE requires three age-appropriate nutrition-literacy topics with food diversity, balanced meal/hydration reasoning, evidence-aware food information and hygiene, misconception handling, assessment, remediation/mastery evidence, explicit child-safety exclusions for dieting/weight/calorie/diagnosis/supplements/allergy self-testing, deterministic QA, offline coverage and release regression coverage.

chapter4Topics.title: Magnetic materials and evidence
competencies: test teacher-provided objects systematically
classify from observed magnetic attraction
distinguish material evidence from appearance
recognise mixed-material objects
misconceptions: all metals are magnetic
shiny objects are magnetic
the outer material always explains attraction
safetyBoundary: teacher/adult-provided classroom objects only
no dismantling powered devices
no high-powered loose magnets

chapter4Topics.title: Magnet poles, attraction and repulsion
competencies: identify two poles
predict like/unlike pole interactions
use repulsion as stronger evidence of two magnets than attraction alone
misconceptions: magnets always attract
every attracted object is a magnet
one observation proves a general rule
safetyBoundary: controlled handling
avoid finger pinch from snapping magnets
ordinary classroom-strength magnets

chapter4Topics.title: Compass direction, interference and safe investigation
competencies: describe roughly north-south settling of a freely rotating magnet
interpret compass deflection from nearby magnetic influence
identify confounding magnetic surroundings
state magnet safety rules
misconceptions: a compass reading cannot be disturbed
nearby magnet movement means geographic north moved
electronics should be dismantled to find magnets
safetyBoundary: never ingest or place magnets in mouth/nose/ears
keep small high-powered magnets away from children
do not dismantle electronics
follow manufacturer or qualified medical guidance around implanted medical devices

chapter4CompletionRule: CHAPTER4_KIKI_TEACHING_SLICE_COMPLETE requires three evidence-led magnet topics covering magnetic-material testing, pole attraction/repulsion and compass/direction reasoning, with misconception handling, linked assessment, remediation/mastery evidence, explicit no-ingestion/no-dismantling/high-powered-magnet safety, deterministic QA, offline coverage and release regression coverage.

chapter5Topics.title: Standard units and reliable length measurement
competencies: choose suitable metric units and instruments
align objects and scales correctly
read at eye level
calculate final minus initial for non-zero starts
misconceptions: the final ruler mark is always the object length
units can be omitted
more decimal places always mean better measurement
safetyBoundary: stable classroom/household objects only
no measurement near traffic or moving machinery
no hot/electrical equipment

chapter5Topics.title: Curved paths, flexible measures and estimation
competencies: choose a flexible method for curved lengths
avoid stretching measuring material
repeat and compare readings
report uncertainty without false precision
misconceptions: a straight chord equals every curved path
repetition creates unlimited precision
an estimate is an exact measurement
safetyBoundary: no cords around the body
no climbing or unstable surfaces
no reaching into moving equipment

chapter5Topics.title: Motion, reference points and patterns
competencies: state a reference point before deciding motion
identify rectilinear/circular/periodic patterns
recognise multiple motion descriptions can coexist
separate motion type from speed or cause
misconceptions: motion is absolute and reference-independent
circular and periodic mean the same thing
motion type alone determines speed
safetyBoundary: toy/tabletop/video observations only
no road or traffic experiments
no chasing/leaning from moving vehicles
no machinery or escalator investigation

chapter5CompletionRule: CHAPTER5_KIKI_TEACHING_SLICE_COMPLETE requires three evidence-led topics covering standard-unit/ruler measurement, curved-length method/uncertainty and reference-aware motion patterns, with misconception handling, linked assessment, remediation/mastery evidence, explicit safe tabletop/classroom measurement and motion boundaries, deterministic QA, offline coverage and release regression coverage.

chapter6Topics.title: Objects, materials and useful classification
competencies: distinguish an object from its material or materials
recognise one object type can use different materials and one material can serve many objects
classify using an explicit consistently applied criterion
misconceptions: object names and material names are interchangeable
similar appearance proves identical material
there is only one valid classification for every purpose
safetyBoundary: intact teacher/adult-provided familiar objects only
no dismantling devices
no scraping coatings or destructive identification

chapter6Topics.title: Appearance, hardness and transparency
competencies: separate observed property from material identity
compare safe samples by appearance and relative hardness
classify transparent/translucent/opaque under stated conditions
recognise sample thickness and surface finish can affect light transmission
misconceptions: shiny means metal
transparent means glass
one observed property uniquely identifies a material
safetyBoundary: non-destructive comparisons only
no knives or broken glass for scratch testing
room light or adult-approved LED only
no lasers or light directed into eyes

chapter6Topics.title: Solubility, floating and choosing materials for a purpose
competencies: distinguish dissolving from floating/sinking
compare known safe samples under controlled water-test conditions
record separate property evidence
justify material choice using multiple relevant properties
misconceptions: floating proves soluble
sinking proves insoluble
tasting is a valid identification method
one attractive property makes a material best for every use
safetyBoundary: known low-risk adult/teacher-provided samples only
no tasting
no unknown powders medicines cleaners or chemicals
no hot water flames broken glass or mains-powered equipment

chapter6CompletionRule: CHAPTER6_KIKI_TEACHING_SLICE_COMPLETE requires three evidence-led topics covering object/material relationships and classification, appearance/hardness/transparency, and solubility versus floating/sinking with purpose-based material choice, including misconception handling, linked assessment, remediation/mastery evidence, explicit no-tasting/no-unknown-chemical/no-sharp-tool/light-safety boundaries, deterministic QA, offline coverage and release regression coverage.

chapter7Topics.title: Temperature, thermal sensation and evidence
competencies: distinguish hot/cold sensation from measured temperature
compare temperatures using instrument evidence
separate measurement from causal or medical interpretation
misconceptions: touch gives exact temperature
feeling cold proves a value below 0 °C
one temperature reading by itself diagnoses illness
safetyBoundary: no touching unknown hot surfaces or liquids
safe moderate-temperature examples or supplied diagrams only
no medical diagnosis or treatment from classroom readings

chapter7Topics.title: Celsius scale, range, least count and defensible precision
competencies: read Celsius scales
calculate least count from equal intervals
distinguish range from resolution
report units and precision supported by the scale
misconceptions: marks and intervals are the same count
range equals least count
more decimal places always mean greater accuracy
safetyBoundary: diagram or intact adult-approved digital thermometer use
no mercury thermometers for learner handling
no handling broken glass or leaked thermometer liquid

chapter7Topics.title: Safe thermometer use, recording and comparison
competencies: choose a suitable thermometer for a safe task
follow instrument placement/range instructions
record time context value and °C
compare repeated readings without overclaiming cause or health meaning
misconceptions: any thermometer suits every task
a single body-temperature reading is a complete diagnosis
bigger temperature changes justify hazardous heating
safetyBoundary: intact adult-approved digital or laboratory-style probes only
no boiling water flames hot cooking vessels or mains heating
body-temperature activities must not diagnose prescribe or delay appropriate care

chapter7CompletionRule: CHAPTER7_KIKI_TEACHING_SLICE_COMPLETE requires three evidence-led topics covering temperature versus sensation, Celsius scale/range/least-count reading and safe thermometer measurement/recording, including misconception handling, linked assessment, remediation/mastery evidence, explicit no-mercury/no-broken-glass/no-boiling-or-flame safety and no-diagnosis claim boundaries, deterministic QA, offline coverage and release regression coverage.

chapter8Topics.title: Solid, liquid and gaseous states of water
competencies: recognise ice liquid water and water vapour as states of the same substance
compare state behaviour using shape flow and container evidence
distinguish invisible water vapour from visible condensed droplets
misconceptions: ice liquid water and vapour are different substances
visible white mist is water vapour itself
appearance alone proves state
safetyBoundary: adult-provided ice room-temperature water or supplied diagrams only
no learner boiling-water or steam-generation activity
no placing hands near hot vapour

chapter8Topics.title: Melting, freezing, evaporation and condensation
competencies: identify four physical state changes from before-and-after evidence
distinguish evaporation from boiling
explain condensation on a cold intact surface
track water through reversible state changes
misconceptions: evaporation requires boiling
evaporated water disappears from existence
outside droplets on a sealed cold bottle must have leaked through
safetyBoundary: room-temperature drying and adult-provided ice/cold-surface examples only
no kettle flame hot plate or sealed-container heating
no learner freezer experiments

chapter8Topics.title: Evaporation, condensation and environmental water evidence
competencies: compare one evaporation factor at a time
interpret supplied evaporation/condensation data
connect state changes cautiously to environmental water movement
state model and evidence limits
misconceptions: one trial proves a universal evaporation rule
a classroom condensation model fully explains weather
faster evaporation justifies unsafe heating
safetyBoundary: supplied data or small room-temperature observations only
no drinking test water or unsafe outdoor collection/climbing
no heat source to accelerate evaporation

chapter8CompletionRule: CHAPTER8_KIKI_TEACHING_SLICE_COMPLETE requires three evidence-led topics covering water states and vapour-versus-droplet distinction, melting/freezing/evaporation/condensation, and fair evidence-aware environmental evaporation/condensation reasoning, with linked assessment, remediation/mastery evidence, explicit no-boiling/no-steam/no-flame/no-hot-plate/no-sealed-heating/no-ingestion safety boundaries, model-limit discipline, deterministic QA, offline coverage and release regression coverage.

chapter9Topics.title: Choosing separation methods from observable mixture properties
competencies: identify mixture components and a usable property difference
choose a method based on size visibility settling solubility or state
distinguish separation from purification and potability
misconceptions: one separation method works for every mixture
ordinary filtration removes dissolved substances
a clear separated liquid is automatically pure or safe to drink
safetyBoundary: known labelled low-risk materials or supplied diagrams/data only
no tasting or smelling unknown mixtures
no medicines cleaners chemicals or drinking separated water

chapter9Topics.title: Handpicking, sieving, winnowing, settling, decantation and filtration
competencies: match common methods to the property difference they use
sequence mechanical and gravity-based methods
state what each method can leave behind
misconceptions: settling or filtration guarantees complete purification
filtration removes dissolved substances and microbes
winnowing requires learner-created dusty powered demonstrations
safetyBoundary: avoid dusty airborne mixtures and unknown powders
no improvised powered fans or mechanical devices
no drinking filtered or decanted samples

chapter9Topics.title: Evaporation and multi-step separation reasoning
competencies: track insoluble and dissolved components through a separation sequence
explain conceptual recovery of a non-volatile dissolved solid through evaporation
state purity potability and evidence limits
misconceptions: filtration removes a dissolved solid
child-operated heating is required to learn evaporation
recovered material is automatically chemically pure
safetyBoundary: supplied diagrams data or adult-prepared examples for evaporation only
no flame kettle hot plate oven microwave improvised electrical heater or sealed-container heating
no evaporation of unknown solutions medicines cleaners or chemicals

chapter9CompletionRule: CHAPTER9_KIKI_TEACHING_SLICE_COMPLETE requires three evidence-led topics covering property-based method choice, common mechanical/gravity separation methods, and conceptual evaporation/multi-step separation, with linked assessment, remediation/mastery evidence, explicit no-tasting/no-unknown-chemical/no-dust-inhalation/no-powered-winnowing/no-hazardous-heating/no-ingestion safety boundaries and separation-versus-purity/potability claim discipline, deterministic QA, offline coverage and release regression coverage.

chapter10Topics.title: Living and non-living characteristics from multiple evidence
competencies: use multiple biological characteristics together
distinguish biological movement from mechanical movement
recognise dormant or low-activity living states
state when evidence is insufficient
misconceptions: anything that moves is alive
anything still is non-living
every living individual must currently reproduce
safetyBoundary: supplied images diagrams records or non-invasive familiar observations only
no wildlife collection handling or nest disturbance
no medical or consciousness classification of people from a classroom life-characteristics checklist

chapter10Topics.title: Seed germination, plant growth and evidence-aware movement
competencies: identify common germination needs for suitable moisture air and temperature
distinguish initial germination from later growth requirements
design or interpret one-factor fair comparisons
recognise slow plant growth responses as biological movement
misconceptions: water alone guarantees germination
light or darkness is a universal germination rule
plants do not move because they do not walk
changing several conditions at once proves one cause
safetyBoundary: known adult-supplied seeds or supplied data only
no tasting experimental seeds or sprouts and no deliberate mould culture
no unknown soil fertilisers chemicals plant damage or wild-plant collection
handwashing after handling growing materials

chapter10Topics.title: Plant and animal life cycles, continuity and change
competencies: order stages from supplied life-cycle evidence
compare developmental change across plants and animals
distinguish shared life-cycle ideas from species-specific stages
state model and timing limits
misconceptions: all species have identical life-cycle stages
every young animal looks like a smaller adult
one diagram gives a universal timetable
organisms must be collected to study life cycles
safetyBoundary: supplied or ethically obtained images recordings and data only
no collection of wild eggs tadpoles larvae cocoons nests or plants
no disturbing habitats or handling unknown animals
no release of classroom-kept organisms into the wild without appropriate expert guidance

chapter10CompletionRule: CHAPTER10_KIKI_TEACHING_SLICE_COMPLETE requires three evidence-led topics covering multi-characteristic living/non-living reasoning, seed germination and plant growth/movement, and comparative plant/animal life cycles, with linked assessment, remediation/mastery evidence, single-characteristic claim discipline, explicit no-tasting/no-deliberate-mould/no-unknown-chemical/no-wildlife-collection/no-habitat-disturbance organism-welfare boundaries, deterministic QA, offline coverage and release regression coverage.
completionRule: SCIENCE_COMPLETE only after all twelve Curiosity chapters have Kiki-teachable coverage, age-appropriate investigations or evidence activities where applicable, practice, assessment, remediation/mastery evidence, accessibility QA and source/provenance review.
